name: Research questions and plans
description: Framing what a piece of research is trying to answer, and planning the sources and searches that could answer it.
l1: Knows a research question should be narrow and that a plan lists the sources to check
l2: Writes a focused question and plan that puts first the sources most likely to answer it; builds a search profile of names, variants, places and known relatives
l3: Plans projects that span several repositories, languages or jurisdictions; revises the plan as findings arrive; pilots the method on a small sample before scaling
l4: Publishes research-planning methods or templates in an edited venue, or ones that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A1.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Reasonably exhaustive search
description: Searching widely enough that the answer is unlikely to be overturned by records not yet seen (GPS element 1), and logging every search, including the misses.
l1: Knows the GPS asks for reasonably exhaustive research and that misses are evidence too
l2: Searches the main catalogues, repositories and platforms for a question; logs every search, including misses
l3: Searches in widening circles (family, community and religious bodies, archives, libraries, overseas collections); normalises search keys across spelling variants, scripts or naming systems; states why the search is reasonably exhaustive
l4: Publishes finding aids, search guides or negative-search evidence in an edited venue, or ones that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A1.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Record access and witness acquisition
description: Finding where records are held and getting copies or images from archives, microfilm, digitisation requests, platforms and private holders. Scope: what a record group contains is Record types and jurisdictions.
l1: Knows records sit in archives, libraries, platforms and private hands, each with its own access terms
l2: Obtains copies or images from archives, platforms and family holders; records where each came from and on what terms
l3: Locates and acquires rare, overseas or restricted witnesses (manuscripts, microfilm, private collections); negotiates with custodians; keeps an inventory of witnesses held and their terms
l4: Brokers access to or digitisation of a collection that an institution then opens to other researchers; advises institutions on access
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A1.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Record types and jurisdictions
description: The record groups for a place and period (civil registration, census, probate, land, church, immigration, military): what each contains, who made it and why. Scope: copies are Record access and witness acquisition; period context is Calendars, places and historical context.
l1: Knows the main record groups for a region and what each typically records
l2: Chooses the record groups that can answer a question for a given place and period; knows what each contains, who created it and why, and its usual gaps
l3: Works across several jurisdictions or record systems; uses the law and administrative practice behind a record to judge what it can prove; traces records moved by boundary and jurisdiction changes
l4: Publishes a record guide for a region or record type in an edited venue or for a repository, or teaches a region's records as course faculty
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A1.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Source, information and evidence classification
description: Judging each source, information item and piece of evidence by its kind (original or derivative, primary or secondary, direct, indirect or negative) before relying on it.
l1: Knows original and derivative sources, primary and secondary information, and direct, indirect and negative evidence
l2: Classifies each source, information item and evidence item before relying on it
l3: Weighs compiled genealogies, transcriptions and machine output by their distance from the event and the informant; treats every transcription as derivative until checked against the image
l4: Publishes evidence-classification methods for new kinds of source in an edited or peer-reviewed venue, or teaches them as course faculty
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A2.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Source citation
description: Citing every source completely and consistently (GPS element 2, layered citations) so anyone can find the exact record and judge it. Scope: carrying citations through an automated pipeline is Claim and provenance modelling.
l1: Knows a citation must let another person find the exact source
l2: Writes complete, consistent citations, including page, image and frame identifiers; puts a citation on every image reproduced
l3: Writes layered citations for derivative and digitised sources (original, film, image, transcription, machine output); cites so that any reader can reach the exact page, image or frame
l4: Sets citation standards that a society, journal or publisher the person does not run adopts, or publishes on citation in an edited venue
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A2.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Provenance and custodial history
description: Tracing a source's creation, custody, transmission and reproduction history, which governs how far it can be trusted. Scope: applying this to zupu editions is Editions, recompilation and witness comparison.
l1: Knows that who made a record, when, and who has held it since affect its weight
l2: Documents a source's creator, date, custody and reproduction history
l3: Reconstructs the transmission history of copied and re-edited works (which copy descends from which); explains differences between witnesses by that history
l4: Publishes provenance studies in an edited venue, or ones that a library or archive uses in its catalogue
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A2.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Palaeography and transcription
description: Reading old handwriting and scripts and transcribing them to stated conventions, marking uncertainty instead of guessing. Scope: any script; Chinese script forms also need Chinese palaeography and variant characters.
l1: Knows transcription conventions: verbatim text, marked gaps and uncertain readings, no silent correction
l2: Transcribes records in at least one script accurately, keeping spelling, punctuation, capitals and marks as written; includes headings, insertions and endorsements; notes damage that affects the reading; marks uncertainty, gaps and the transcriber's own comments; never fills a gap from expectation
l3: Reads difficult hands, damaged pages and unusual layouts; settles uncertain characters with named, checkable evidence; checks other people's and machines' transcriptions
l4: Recognised authority on a script or record type: holds a palaeography qualification, teaches palaeography as course faculty, or sets transcription conventions that an archive, society or publication the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A3.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Abstracting and structured extraction
description: Turning records into structured abstracts (people, relationships, dates, places), each pointing back to its source.
l1: Knows the difference between a transcription, an abstract and an extract
l2: Abstracts records into structured fields (person, relationship, date, place) with a pointer back to the source, keeping the meaning, quoting ambiguous wording, leaving out boilerplate and marking any comment as the abstractor's
l3: Designs extraction schemas from a record type's entry anatomy; handles entries that do not fit the schema without forcing them
l4: Designs extraction standards that collections or projects the person does not run adopt
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A3.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Calendars, places and historical context
description: Placing records in time and place: calendar and era-date conversion, historical jurisdictions, gazetteers and migration context. Scope: includes all calendar conversion; Chinese reference data is Chinese historical reference databases.
l1: Knows that dates and place names change over time and must be read in period context
l2: Converts dates between calendars, including regnal and era dates; identifies historical places and jurisdictions; uses period context to interpret a record
l3: Handles ambiguous dates, renamed or abolished places and period-specific terms; keeps place and migration notes that others can check
l4: Publishes reference tools (converters, gazetteers, chronologies) in an edited venue, or ones that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A3.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Record languages and translation
description: Reading and translating records in their original language: Latin, older vernaculars, classical languages and formulaic legal wording. Scope: script forms are Palaeography and transcription; Chinese register and titles are Translation register and annotation; machine translation is Machine translation pipelines.
l1: Knows the record languages of the regions and periods they research, and when a translation is needed
l2: Reads and translates standard records in at least one record language that is not their own modern language (e.g. Latin parish entries, older legal forms of their own language, classical Chinese) with a glossary
l3: Handles legal, abbreviated and formulaic language; checks other people's and machines' translations
l4: Publishes translations or record-language guides in an edited venue, or teaches record languages as course faculty
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A3.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Analysis and correlation of evidence
description: Correlating evidence from several sources, in tables or timelines, to test what the records together support (GPS element 3).
l1: Knows evidence must be compared across sources, not read one source at a time
l2: Correlates evidence from several sources in tables or timelines to test a hypothesis
l3: Correlates large or conflicting bodies of evidence; recognises when apparent agreement comes from shared dependence on one source
l4: Teaches correlation methods as course faculty, or reviews analyses for a journal, credentialing body or society
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A4.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Identity resolution and kinship determination
description: Establishing who is who and who is related to whom: same-name problems, merges and splits, and parent-child proof, including research in one person's FAN cluster (family, friends, associates, neighbours). Scope: studying a defined group is Prosopography and cluster research.
l1: Knows that the same name is not the same person and that each parent-child link needs its own evidence
l2: Separates or merges individuals on evidence; uses associates and neighbours to separate or identify individuals; documents parent-child links across three generations
l3: Resolves hard identity cases (common names, aliases, adoption, name changes), including through structured cluster research; keeps birth and adoptive lineages distinct; avoids false merges and false splits at scale
l4: Publishes identity or kinship solutions in a peer-reviewed journal, or designs identity-resolution methods that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A4.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Conflict resolution and proof arguments
description: Resolving conflicting evidence and writing the proof summary or proof argument behind a conclusion (GPS elements 4 and 5).
l1: Knows conflicting evidence must be resolved or explained, not ignored
l2: Writes a proof summary that resolves a conflict and reaches a conclusion on the strongest evidence
l3: Writes proof arguments for indirect- and conflicting-evidence problems; states what would overturn the conclusion; holds a question open when evidence is insufficient
l4: Publishes proof arguments in peer-reviewed journals; reviews others' proofs for a journal or credentialing body
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A4.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Genetic genealogy evidence
description: Using DNA test results (autosomal, Y-DNA, mtDNA, shared matches) as evidence alongside documents, within what the tests can show.
l1: Knows the test types (autosomal, Y-DNA, mtDNA) and what each can and cannot show
l2: Uses DNA matches and shared-centimorgan ranges to test a documentary hypothesis; knows Y-DNA can test a documented paternal line
l3: Correlates DNA with documentary evidence in proof arguments, including Y-DNA tests of documented paternal lines; handles endogamy and misattributed parentage; follows informed-consent rules for testers
l4: Publishes DNA case studies in a peer-reviewed venue, or contributes to genetic-genealogy standards that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A4.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Prosopography and cluster research
description: Studying a defined group (a lineage, a cohort of officials or graduates, a parish or migrant community) and the ties among its members. Scope: identifying one person by their cluster is Identity resolution and kinship determination; CBDB stays under Chinese historical reference databases.
l1: Knows what prosopography is and when a question concerns a group rather than one person
l2: Builds a group list from records with each member's source; maps the ties among members (e.g. witnesses, sponsors, neighbours, co-migrants)
l3: Defines a population with explicit inclusion rules, records each member's identification evidence, and draws group conclusions that state their coverage and limits (e.g. officeholders, a parish, a migrant cohort; quantitative tests where the numbers support them)
l4: Publishes prosopographical work in an edited or peer-reviewed venue, or builds a reference population that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A4.5); description: drafted for the graph

name: Privacy of living persons and consent
description: Protecting living people's information: what may be shared, with whose consent, at what level of detail, through release tiers. Scope: enforcing the policy automatically is Privacy-safe AI pipelines and release.
l1: Knows living people's data needs protection and that the law differs by jurisdiction
l2: Withholds or redacts living people's details from shared work unless they have consented
l3: Sets release tiers by recency and surface (private, internal, redacted, public); records consent for specific passages; checks for harm to living relatives through inference
l4: Sets privacy policy that a society, platform or archive adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A5.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Copyright, licensing and terms of use
description: Respecting rights in images, data and publications: copyright, licences and the terms of record platforms.
l1: Knows images, transcriptions and databases carry rights and terms of use
l2: Checks terms before reusing images or data; licenses own work explicitly
l3: Separates rights layers (third-party sources, own research, code); documents each source's redistribution status; clears permissions for publication
l4: Advises institutions or societies other than their own on rights policy
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A5.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Family collaboration, testimony and cultural respect
description: Working with family members and communities: recording oral testimony with who said it and when, crediting collaborators, using community archives, and respecting cultural traditions.
l1: Knows family testimony is evidence with its own strengths and limits, and that communities have a stake in their records
l2: Records testimony with who said it and when; credits collaborators; keeps testimony distinct from documented fact
l3: Defines the scope of each informant's authority; runs correction and consent processes with family and community bodies (e.g. family associations, clans, congregations); follows a community's own rules for its data before putting records through AI tools; labels tradition and cultural claims as such
l4: Is recognised by a community body, society or archive the person does not run for leading community genealogy work across families or associations, or publishes on community practice in an edited venue
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A5.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Professional practice and client work
description: Doing research for clients: written agreements on scope, fees and deliverables, professional codes of conduct, confidentiality, and reports a client can act on. Scope: commissioned work; the research craft itself sits in the research and evidence competencies.
l1: Knows the professional codes (e.g. APG, BCG) and that client work needs an agreed scope, fee and report
l2: Agrees scope, fees and deliverables in writing; delivers a research report a client can act on, which starts from what was already known and reports what was searched and not found; keeps client data confidential
l3: Runs several commissions at once; reports inconclusive results and their limits plainly; handles conflicts of interest, scope changes and disputes
l4: Serves as a judge, examiner or ethics officer for a professional body, or teaches professional practice as course faculty
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A5.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Genealogical data modelling
description: Modelling genealogical data (persons, relationships, unions, events, sources) while keeping what records say apart from conclusions. Scope: recording machine-produced claims and their review state is Claim and provenance modelling.
l1: Knows the core entities: person, relationship, union, event, source and citation
l2: Records data in a genealogy database or spreadsheet with a source linked to each fact
l3: Designs schemas for hard cases (adoption recorded so that both birth and adoptive lineages remain traceable, plural marriage, succession and heirship, variant accounts across sources); keeps source attestations separate from conclusions
l4: Designs data models that projects or tools the person does not run adopt
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A6.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Genealogy software and data exchange
description: Using genealogy software and platforms (such as Gramps or FamilySearch) and moving data between tools through GEDCOM 7, GEDCOM X and other formats without silent loss.
l1: Knows GEDCOM and the main genealogy programs and platforms
l2: Exports and imports GEDCOM between tools and checks what was lost
l3: Writes and validates exports to an exchange standard (e.g. GEDCOM 7) from any tool or database, mapping non-standard data (extensions, non-Latin names, variants) without silent loss
l4: Contributes accepted changes to exchange standards, or to widely used genealogy tools the person does not run
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A6.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Genealogical writing and narrative
description: Writing up research: proof summaries, compiled genealogies and family histories that keep fact and inference distinct.
l1: Knows the standard forms: proof summary, research report, compiled genealogy, family history
l2: Writes a research report or family sketch with citations, in a format accepted in the field, with a clear line between fact and inference; places the family in its historical and community setting
l3: Writes book-length family history that keeps uncertainty visible; uses a numbering system; labels each claim by its basis (e.g. documented, inferred, traditional)
l4: Publishes family history in edited or peer-reviewed venues, or holds an award for it from a body the person does not run
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A7.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Book and archive production
description: Producing finished publications in print or on the web (typesetting, ISBN, legal deposit) that meet each surface's obligations. Scope: regenerating outputs automatically is Derived outputs and release engineering.
l1: Knows the publication surfaces (print, PDF, website, database) and their obligations
l2: Produces a print-ready or web publication from structured sources
l3: Produces book and web editions that meet publication obligations (identifiers such as ISBN, legal deposit, rights notices); typesets non-Latin scripts where needed; checks every surface against the data before release
l4: Sets production standards that a publisher, society or series adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A7.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Corrections, revision and continuation
description: Keeping published work right over time: correction logs, errata, revised editions and continuing the lineage.
l1: Knows published genealogy needs a way to correct errors and add new generations
l2: Keeps a correction log; issues errata and dated revisions
l3: Runs a revision protocol: correction intake, re-review, versioned releases and continuation of the lineage in later editions
l4: Designs revision or continuation processes that a society, family association or long-running project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (A7.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: AI research assistants and search
description: Using AI chat assistants, record hints, full-text search and document summaries to find leads, and checking each against the record itself. Scope: one's own research; building pipelines is Agentic workflow design and the agent competencies after it.
l1: Knows chat assistants and AI search tools can find, summarise and misstate records, and that their answers are leads to check
l2: Uses AI search, record hints, full-text search of handwritten records and document summaries to find leads; checks each against the record itself before relying on it; cites the record, not the assistant
l3: Chooses AI tools by tested reliability for a record type, allowing for what a tool was trained on and whom it under-represents; designs prompts and checks that expose invented records and citations; records which tool produced each lead
l4: Teaches responsible AI-assisted research as course faculty, or publishes evaluations of AI research tools in an edited venue
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (C1.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Multi-witness machine transcription
description: Producing machine transcriptions with OCR, handwriting recognition or vision-language models, and checking them against independent readings. Scope: ruling on a contested reading is Independent review and adjudication.
l1: Knows machine transcription of historical text has high error rates and can invent content
l2: Produces a machine transcription and lists its divergences from at least one independent check (a second engine or a human pass)
l3: Chooses or trains engines by measured accuracy for each script and layout; counts agreement between similarly trained models as one witness; routes readings that would change a claim to a reader qualified in the script
l4: Publishes transcription pipelines, trained models or results in an edited venue, or ones that a body or project the person does not run adopts as a benchmark
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (C2.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Machine translation pipelines
description: Running machine translation with parallel renderings and glossary control, checked independently. Scope: the translator's own skill is Record languages and translation (and Translation register and annotation for Chinese).
l1: Knows machine translation can drop or invent content and flatten terms
l2: Checks machine translations against a glossary and at least one independent check (a second rendering or a human reader)
l3: Builds translation pipelines that record disagreements between renderings, apply glossary and naming rules automatically and link each translation to the transcription version it came from; routes disputed meanings to a qualified translator
l4: Sets translation-pipeline standards that projects or publishers the person does not run adopt
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (C2.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Independent review and adjudication
description: Reviewing machine output against the source and ruling on contested readings by written rules, measuring reviewer agreement. Scope: ruling in person needs L2 in that script and language (Palaeography and transcription, Record languages and translation; for Chinese, also Chinese palaeography and variant characters).
l1: Knows machine output is a proposal until a person reviews it
l2: Reviews agent output against the source image and records a judgement for each item, within the scripts and languages they can read
l3: Designs independent review with recorded evidence; sends contested readings to reviewers qualified in the script and language and has them decided by declared rules; escalates to the project's editorial authority (editor, family body or client) where needed; measures reviewer agreement
l4: Designs review and adjudication protocols that projects the person does not run adopt
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (C3.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: AI disclosure and use boundaries
description: Being open about what AI did: disclosing and citing AI's part in the work, and keeping within the AI rules of clients, professional bodies, publishers and platforms.
l1: Knows the principles of responsible AI use in their field: accuracy, disclosure, privacy, education and compliance
l2: Discloses where AI materially shaped the work and records which AI tools were used; cites an AI response where its words are kept; never presents AI-generated or AI-altered material as evidence
l3: Writes an AI-use statement for a project or product saying what agents did and what people verified; checks the AI rules of clients, credentialing bodies, publishers and platforms before delivering
l4: Contributes to AI guidelines or position statements that a professional body, society or coalition publishes
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (C5.1), the agentic field's shared Mandatory wording; description: drafted for the graph

name: Privacy and data protection in AI use
description: Controlling what reaches a model: keeping personal and confidential data out of prompts, checking providers' data terms, and automatic redaction and release checks.
l1: Knows that data sent to a model provider can leave their control, and what a provider's data terms cover
l2: Keeps personal and confidential data out of prompts unless it is permitted; checks a provider's data terms before sending records
l3: Builds redaction and release checks into the workflow and enforces the policy automatically
l4: Designs privacy arrangements for AI use that projects or organisations the person does not run adopt
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (C5.2), the agentic field's shared Mandatory wording; description: drafted for the graph

name: Zupu genre and anatomy
description: Understanding the Chinese genealogy (zupu) as a genre: its parts, compilation rules and how charts and entries refer to each other.
l1: Knows what a zupu is and its usual parts: prefaces, compilation rules, charts, entries, regulations, tombs and property
l2: Reads a zupu cold: identifies its parts and compilation rules and how charts and entries refer to each other
l3: Reads unusual or damaged zupu and their back matter (contracts, honours, testaments, donor rosters); interprets entries by the compiler's own rules; explains the politics behind prefaces
l4: Recognised authority on the zupu genre: publishes on it in an edited or peer-reviewed venue
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B1.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Editions, recompilation and witness comparison
description: Identifying zupu editions (manuscript and print), finding other editions, and collating them to establish what each adds or changes. Scope: the general method is Provenance and custodial history; automated person matching is Lineage reconciliation and variant tracking.
l1: Knows zupu were recompiled and recopied, so one lineage can have several editions
l2: Identifies a zupu's edition and finds other editions in catalogues (Shanghai Library, FamilySearch, university libraries)
l3: Compares editions entry by entry; classifies divergences by cause (copying error, deliberate revision, new information); counts editions as independent witnesses only when their history shows they are
l4: Publishes edition studies or catalogues in an edited venue, or ones that a library adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B1.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Lineage, branch and generation systems
description: Placing people in a lineage's branches and generations, using generation names and sibling name sets as checks.
l1: Knows generation numbering, branches and houses, and generation poems
l2: Places a person in the right generation and branch; uses generation characters and sibling name sets as checks
l3: Aligns generation counts across branches and editions; links persons across pages and branches from the compiler's own cross-reference conventions (e.g. literary-name references) when generation characters do not settle it
l4: Publishes generation-alignment or disambiguation methods in an edited venue, or ones that a body or project the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B1.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Genealogical formulae and kinship terms
description: Reading the formulae and kinship terms of zupu entries: wives, children, adoption, succession and burial.
l1: Knows the common entry formulae (配, 子 with a count, 字, 號, 葬)
l2: Reads standard entries correctly, including wives, children, succession and burial formulae
l3: Treats adoption and succession (嗣, 過繼, 兼祧) as distinct relationship types; reads honorific and taboo conventions that change meaning; settles formula ambiguity from the compiler's rules
l4: Publishes formula glossaries or reference guides in an edited venue, or ones that a library or research guide the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B2.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Chinese palaeography and variant characters
description: Reading Chinese script in zupu: variant and cursive characters, taboo forms and vertical layout. Scope: ruling in person on a Chinese reading under Independent review and adjudication needs L2 here.
l1: Knows vertical right-to-left reading, variant characters and cursive forms
l2: Reads printed and clear manuscript zupu; marks uncertain glyphs instead of guessing
l3: Reads cursive, damaged and variant forms; settles hard characters from their components with the evidence recorded; recognises taboo-avoidance forms and copyist confusions
l4: Recognised palaeographic authority for a period or region: publishes in an edited venue, teaches as course faculty, or is consulted by libraries
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B2.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Chinese names and romanisation
description: Recording Chinese personal names of every type and romanising them consistently, including dialect forms.
l1: Knows the name types (given, courtesy, literary, posthumous) and that romanisation systems differ
l2: Records each name type in its own field; romanises consistently to a declared standard (e.g. Hanyu Pinyin, ALA-LC, Jyutping); keeps dialect romanisations as their own forms
l3: Resolves names across editions and name types; keeps name-variant lists; labels provisional readings of polyphonic characters; follows a declared rule for rendering personal names (romanise, gloss or translate)
l4: Sets naming and romanisation conventions that a library, catalogue or publisher adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B2.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Translation register and annotation
description: Translating zupu entries in a declared register (documentary or readable), annotating official titles, kinship terms and allusions. Scope: other record languages are Record languages and translation; machine translation is Machine translation pipelines.
l1: Knows classical Chinese is terse and that renderings of titles and kin terms vary
l2: Translates entries in a declared register with a glossary of titles and kin terms; keeps the Chinese beside the English
l3: Keeps literal and readable translations separate and checkable against each other; renders official titles to a cited standard (e.g. Hucker); annotates dates, places, figures and allusions
l4: Publishes translations in an edited venue, or translation standards that a body or publisher the person does not run adopts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B2.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Chinese historical reference databases
description: Corroborating offices, places and dates with Chinese historical reference databases (CBDB, CHGIS) and local gazetteers. Scope: calendar conversion is Calendars, places and historical context; group studies are Prosopography and cluster research.
l1: Knows the main reference databases and that local gazetteers record officials and examination graduates
l2: Queries reference databases and gazetteers to corroborate offices, places and dates
l3: Matches persons to biographical databases with explicit identity criteria; uses historical GIS for places and migration; records misses as negative evidence
l4: Contributes data or methods that a reference database accepts
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B3.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Lineage institutions and origin traditions
description: Understanding lineage institutions (ancestral halls, corporate estates, lineage rules) and treating surname-origin traditions critically.
l1: Knows lineages were institutions with halls, estates and rules, and that origin claims reach into legend
l2: Interprets halls, estates, rules and rituals in a zupu; labels surname-origin claims as traditional or legendary
l3: Explains how lineages constructed descent for status and property; keeps legend, tradition and documented descent apart in conclusions; handles patrilineal and diaspora framing with care
l4: Recognised authority on Chinese lineage history: publishes in an edited or peer-reviewed venue
source: L1-L4: chan-agen.md (B3.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Agentic workflow design
description: Designing agent workflows for research tasks: stages, contracts between stages, and points where people review the output.
l1: Knows an agent pipeline needs defined inputs, outputs, limits and a human review point
l2: Runs a defined agent workflow on a task (e.g. transcribe and translate a page) with a template and a review step
